characters: Children in school uniforms using a tap, a covered bucket, a clean drain and a pot of boiled water with an adult nearby.

narrationPlan.voice: Clear, encouraging voice; each habit is said with a firm, friendly beat
narrationPlan.pace: Steady, like a marching chant (about 75 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A steady marching beat with a chorus that repeats “Every drop counts” (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Water matters for every home, farm and school in Ghana, and many families fetch water from taps, wells, boreholes or streams. This song uses simple habits that any child can start.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Check that the habits (closing the tap, covering stored water, keeping drains clear, boiling or filtering drinking water) are accurate and safe.
Confirm that children are not asked to handle boiling water; an adult does it.

teacherGuide.overview: A water-care song with six habits. Form: six couplets. Rhyming pairs: bird/herd, teeth/beneath, too/through, drain/rain, drink/think, share/there. It builds responsibility and links water with health.
learningGoals: Name four ways to look after water.
Say why clean water matters for health.
beforeReading: Ask: where does your water come from at home?
whileReading: Use a pretend tap, lid and bin to act each habit.
afterReading: Make a poster of one water habit.
Check the school taps and report any that drip, to an adult.
discussion: Why must drinking water be clean?
What happens if rubbish blocks a drain?
reflection: Which habit will you try this week?

mathsExtension.task: A tap drips one cup of water every hour. How many cups drip in a school day of 6 hours?

support: Act the song with simple props and let children choose one habit to show.
stretch: Write a new couplet about one more way to save water.

culturalNotes: Water matters for every home, farm and school in Ghana, and many families fetch water from taps, wells, boreholes or streams. This song uses simple habits that any child can start.
localiseThis: Use the local water sources (tap, well, borehole or stream) that children know.
Keep children away from boiling water and open wells and streams.

factCheck.explanation: Confirm the safe-water advice with the local health or water authority.
